Show an overlay created on the server

Source: R/dialog-server.R
shad_show_dialog.Rd

Build a shad_dialog() (or alert dialog, sheet, drawer) in the server function and show it, the way shiny::showModal() works — no need to place it in the UI up front and no trigger.

Usage

shad_show_dialog(
  overlay,
  transient = TRUE,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

overlay

A shad_dialog(), shad_alert_dialog(), shad_sheet(), or shad_drawer() tag.

transient

If TRUE (default), the overlay is destroyed and removed from the document once it closes. If FALSE, it stays in the document and can be reopened with shad_dialog_open().

session

The Shiny session.

Value

Invisibly the overlay's input id.

Details

The overlay is inserted at the end of <body>, opens itself once its JavaScript instance exists, and by default removes itself from the document after it closes (transient = TRUE). Its inputs are live while it is open — read input$<id> inside it as usual — so transient = FALSE is the right call when you need those values to survive the close.

Because the tag is built in the server, its ids are namespaced by the module that built it exactly like any other UI; shad_remove_dialog() takes the unnamespaced id.

See also

shad_dialog_open(), shad_remove_dialog()

Other shadshiny server API: shad_message_scroller_to_bottom(), shad_overlay_server, shad_remove_dialog(), shad_toast(), update_shad, update_shad_command()

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  server <- function(input, output, session) {
    shiny::observeEvent(input$open, {
      shad_show_dialog(shad_dialog(
        "confirm", title = "Delete project?",
        description = "This cannot be undone.",
        footer = shad_dialog_close_button()
      ))
    })
  }
}
